About Brian / Overview
Brian Zhou Liu (goes by Brian Liu) is a data science student at UC San Diego. He loves tinkering with data, software, and research. You can find him building hackathon projects, training models, or exploring San Diego in the sun.

chunks.heading: Q-Lab, UC San Diego (Research Intern, Jan 2026 to present)
chunks.text:
Brian's experience / Q-Lab, UC San Diego (Research Intern, Jan 2026 to present)
Research Intern under Prof. Lianhui Qin in La Jolla, CA. Building and evaluating AI systems for scientific simulation and single-cell forecasting. Co-developed SIGA, a Claude Code adapter that configures scientific simulators; built its ChromaDB retrieval layer, MCP XML validator, and plugin framework, and co-authored the accompanying preprint (https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.09774). Led a 30-task OpenFOAM transfer study; SIGA's best configuration scored 0.870 accuracy with 30/30 complete cases. On harder held-out GEOS tasks, SIGA raised accuracy by 9.6% from 0.720 to 0.789 and reduced run-to-run standard deviation by about 16x. Also developed a direct encoder-decoder Transformer to forecast four future single-cell states from 100,000 trajectories, reaching R² = 0.536 across 3,201 output genes and R² = 0.857 on the top 50 dynamic genes.

chunks.heading: Asakana, YC F26 (Product Development Intern, Oct 2025 to Feb 2026)
chunks.text:
Brian's experience / Asakana, YC F26 (Product Development Intern, Oct 2025 to Feb 2026)
Remote. Automated supplier data entry and built an AI-assisted ordering system. Deployed a first-generation OCR/ETL pipeline with Gemini Flash-Lite, automating previously manual supplier entry for 10,000+ products from PDF and Excel sheets into MongoDB. Developed a Dialogflow CX ordering agent backed by Cloud SQL and REST APIs, with Twilio SMS notifications and automated pricing-rule enforcement.

chunks.heading: Rare AI Lab, UC San Diego (Research Intern, Sep 2024 to Dec 2025)
chunks.text:
Brian's experience / Rare AI Lab, UC San Diego (Research Intern, Sep 2024 to Dec 2025)
Research Intern under Prof. Aobo Li in La Jolla, CA. Developed surrogate models that made detector-design optimization cheaper to run. Implemented a multi-fidelity surrogate optimizer combining conditional neural processes and Gaussian processes, reducing detector-simulation cost by 90% for experimental design exploration. Co-first-authored "Efficient Optimization of COHERENT Detector Design Parameters with RESuM," accepted to the NeurIPS 2025 ML4PS Workshop.

chunks.heading: MAIX Lab, Emory University (Research Intern, Mar 2023 to Nov 2023)
chunks.text:
Brian's experience / MAIX Lab, Emory University (Research Intern, Mar 2023 to Nov 2023)
Research Intern and Regeneron STS Top 300 Scholar under Prof. Ran Xiao in Atlanta, GA. Built deep-learning models for cardiac screening from ECG data. Constructed an anatomically informed feature tensor for cardiac screening using XResNet, achieving 93.7% AUC. Boosted model sensitivity to 85.5% with 1D convolutional layers that capture cross-lead patterns.

chunks.heading: FlashMath (2026, independent project)
chunks.text:
Brian's projects / FlashMath (2026, independent project)
AI-assisted math study desktop app. Built with Tauri, Rust, React, and TypeScript. A cross-platform study app with local persistence, screenshot and PDF ingestion, LaTeX rendering, provider-agnostic AI OCR, and an exam-aware version of the SM-2 review algorithm. Code: https://github.com/brianzliu/FlashMath

chunks.heading: Blueprint (Jan 2026, NexHacks, 1st place DevTools)
chunks.text:
Brian's projects / Blueprint (Jan 2026, NexHacks, 1st place DevTools)
Codebase summarization and vulnerability detection. Built with TypeScript, React Flow, D3.js, AST parsing, Gemini, and bear-1. A VS Code extension that extracts repository structure, maps file dependencies, summarizes code at multiple levels, and flags security risks. Tested on repositories as large as MongoDB. Devpost: https://devpost.com/software/unnamed-pzmyes

chunks.heading: CARP (Oct 2025, Sushi Hackathon at Stanford, 3rd place)
chunks.text:
Brian's projects / CARP (Oct 2025, Sushi Hackathon at Stanford, 3rd place)
Health monitoring and catch optimization system. Built with Arduino, Python, Bluetooth, Random Forest, and RAG. An FSR-402 pressure-sensing brace with Bluetooth telemetry, live carpal-tunnel risk scores, alerts, historical trends, and a fishing dashboard built around more than 50,000 geospatial data points. Slides: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1G8c4U542EkD4S2SwFdJhdvmzZ8a2mNtRQ0Zzb5SSXFg/edit?slide=id.g388d26c538d_3_786

chunks.heading: Bouncer (Jun 2025, Berkeley AI Hackathon)
chunks.text:
Brian's projects / Bouncer (Jun 2025, Berkeley AI Hackathon)
Malicious actor prevention system. Built with React Native, Supabase, Claude, Gemini, and Google Search. An access-control dashboard that searches public records from signup data, produces an explained risk score, and alerts administrators when a user crosses a configurable threshold. Devpost: https://devpost.com/software/bouncer-7cvsgz

chunks.heading: CiteTrace (May 2025, ACM x Intel Hackathon, 1st place)
chunks.text:
Brian's projects / CiteTrace (May 2025, ACM x Intel Hackathon, 1st place)
Research knowledge graph. Built with React Native, TypeScript, D3.js, RAG, and Supabase. An interactive graph that connects uploaded academic work, explains relationships between papers, and lets researchers query their literature with grounded citations. Devpost: https://devpost.com/software/inciteful

chunks.heading: PillSnap (Apr 2025, UCSD DiamondHacks, Best Use of Auth0)
chunks.text:
Brian's projects / PillSnap (Apr 2025, UCSD DiamondHacks, Best Use of Auth0)
AI-powered pill identifier. Built with Gemini, Vertex AI, the FDA API, Cloud Run, and Vercel. A pill-identification app that combines image descriptions with FDA data, saves medication details, and surfaces drug and food interaction warnings. Devpost: https://devpost.com/software/pill-snap

chunks.heading: Low-Cost Blind Navigation Apparatus (Sep 2022 to Feb 2023, independent research)
chunks.text:
Brian's projects / Low-Cost Blind Navigation Apparatus (Sep 2022 to Feb 2023, independent research)
Wearable computer-vision navigation aid. Built with Python, OpenCV, YOLOv4-tiny, and a Raspberry Pi. A Raspberry Pi head-worn navigation system with real-time audio feedback. Its object detector reached 87.34% mAP while reducing hardware cost by about 90% against commercial alternatives.
